query: accepted-entry exit timing MFE giveback trading survival analysis triple barrier meta labeling profit taking trailing stop offline policy evaluation
content:
**Accepted-entry timing** refers to choosing precise entry points (e.g., after a confirmation, retest, or volatility spike) to maximize MFE while minimizing MAE and giveback. Poor timing inflates early givebacks; better timing aligns with statistical MFE/MAE peaks. [[9]](https://www.forexfactory.com/thread/516681-does-timing-of-entry-really-matter-or-just?page=2) [[10]](https://journalplus.co/metrics/maximum-adverse-excursion)

### Key Frameworks and Tools for Analysis
1. **MFE/Giveback + Survival Analysis**:
   - Track duration to MFE/MAE (e.g., many losers hit MFE in <5 minutes, but winners need longer). Plot MFE vs. time-to-MFE or time-to-close for exit optimization. [[6]](https://www.tradesviz.com/blog/mfe-mae-duration/)
   - Use to set time-based profit-taking (e.g., exit after median MFE duration) or trailing stops. Survival models predict “how long until giveback risk spikes.”
   - Example: If average MFE is 2.4R but you exit early, survival curves show high giveback probability—switch to trailing or longer targets. [[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g7rvyaiOm7g)

2. **Triple-Barrier Labeling (with Meta-Labeling)**:
   - Primary model (e.g., Bollinger bands for side) generates signals.
   - Triple barriers label outcomes for ML (Random Forest or similar) to decide “trade or skip”—meta-labeling.
   - Improves signal efficacy by filtering noisy trades and incorporating realistic exits. Backtests on futures (e.g., S&P E-mini) show better risk-adjusted performance. [[11]](https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/) [[1]](https://www.newsletter.quantreo.com/p/the-triple-barrier-labeling-of-marco)
   - Combines naturally with MFE/MAE for dynamic barriers.

3. **Profit Taking + Trailing Stops via Offline Evaluation**:
   - Simulate policies offline: e.g., take-profit at 50–80% of MFE (exit efficiency), or trailing stop after profit target.
   - Use survival/hazard models to choose thresholds that minimize giveback (premature reversals).
   - Trailing stops protect profits dynamically; offline eval compares capture rates vs. giveback risk (e.g., 55–70% capture is often optimal). [[12]](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/t/trailingstop.asp) [[13]](https://journalplus.co/metrics/max-runup)
   - For accepted-entry timing: Select entries with favorable MFE/MAE ratios; offline eval tests retest or confirmation rules.

### Practical Workflow (Meta-Labeling + Survival for Survival of Trades)
- **Data**: Historical bars/prices.
- **Step 1**: Apply triple barriers to label data (upper = TP, lower = SL, vertical = time).
- **Step 2**: Add meta-labeler (ML model on features like RSI, volatility) to predict trade success.
- **Step 3**: Incorporate MFE/MAE/survival:
  - Compute duration to MFE/MAE.
  - Model time-to-event (Cox proportional hazards or similar) for giveback risk.
  - Evaluate exits offline: e.g., “If I use trailing stop after X% MFE with Y-hour time barrier, what is expected return/survival probability?”
- **Step 4**: Optimize for accepted-entry timing—filter entries where MFE > MAE ratio is high, or use duration stats for volatility-adjusted entries.
- **Implementation Notes**: Tools like mlfinlab (Python) handle triple-barrier + meta-labeling; TradesViz/TradingView scripts for MFE/MAE duration; survival in Python (lifelines or statsmodels). Backtest with out-of-sample validation to avoid overfitting.

### Benefits and Evidence
- Reduces giveback/leakage (many traders exit <60% of MFE; pros target >80%). [[3]](https://journalplus.co/learn/guides/mae-mfe-guide)
- Better risk control: Triple barriers + survival handle path dependency (trades don’t end at fixed times).
- Offline policy evaluation enables safe experimentation (e.g., “Would this new trailing rule survive 70% of historical givebacks?”).
- Real-world validation: Combinations improve primary strategy performance on equities/futures; survival analysis extends technical signals for stock trading. [[11]](https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/) [[2]](https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/compec/v64y2024i6d10.1007_s10614-024-10567-8.html)

This is not a complete backtesting script (requires historical data), but it directly addresses your query. For implementation, start with Lopez de Prado’s framework (triple barriers) + MFE/MAE tools for exits, and survival models for duration-based profit-taking. If you have specific assets, parameters, or code needs, provide more details for deeper tailoring!

## Meta-labelling [...] ## The Triple Barrier Method (TBM)

To overcome the challenges we discussed above, de Prado introduces a labelling technique known as the triple barrier method.

The triple barrier method involves “labelling an observation according to the first barrier touched of out three barriers… two horizontal barriers and one vertical barrier”.

An example of the Triple Barrier Method (de Prado, 47)

The horizontal barriers can be thought of as profit-taking or stop-loss limits. Rather than setting a fixed threshold, de Prado recommends using a dynamic function that calculates a rolling threshold based on daily volatility. extra_sources.description:
In short, the Triple Barrier Method transforms raw directional signals into a reliable training set for smarter decision-making.

  

Thanks for reading Quantreo! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

Subscribe

Most traders label their data in a simplistic way, and wonder why their models don’t work.

The Triple Barrier Method changes the game.

It adds _realism_ to your backtests by mimicking what would actually happen in a trade:

Take-profit, stop-loss, or timeout.

And if you’re building advanced workflows like meta-labelling, it’s not optional —

it’s the backbone that allows your meta-model to learn from real trade outcomes, not noisy price shifts.

👉 Start using it today with just a few lines of code in the quantreo library. [...] ## 3. Why It’s a Perfect Fit for Meta-Labelling

The Triple Barrier Method is a natural foundation for building meta-labels.

In meta-labelling, your goal isn’t to predict the market directly — it's to decide whether to act on a primary signal (long/short). But to do that, your model needs feedback on how those signals typically end.

That’s exactly what the triple barrier provides.

It gives each entry signal a structured label:

   `+1` if the trade would have reached take-profit,

   `-1` if it would have hit the stop-loss,

   `0` if it expired before reaching either.

This clear outcome gives your meta-model a concrete objective: learn to filter out bad signals, and only act on those with a higher chance of success. [...] Subscribe

  

## 1. What Is the Triple Barrier Method?

The Triple Barrier Method, introduced by Marcos López de Prado, is a powerful way to label trading data.

Instead of checking whether the price goes up or down after _n_ candles, it simulates realistic trade conditions using three key barriers:

### 🟢 1. Upper Barrier → Take Profit

Set at a fixed percentage or return above the entry price.

If the price hits this level first, the trade is labeled as +1 (profit).

### 🔴 2. Lower Barrier → Stop Loss

Placed below the entry price.

If this level is reached first, the label is -1 (loss).

### ⏱ 3. Vertical Barrier → Max Holding Time

If neither TP nor SL is hit within a certain number of periods, the trade expires, and the label is 0 (neutral).

Advances in Financial Machine Learning, Snippet 3.6 page 50.

Getting the Time of the First Touch, with Meta Labels

This function is orchestrator to meta-label the data, in conjunction with the Triple Barrier Method.

#### Parameters¶

close pd.Series
Close prices

t_events pd.Series
of t_events. These are timestamps that will seed every triple barrier. These are the timestamps selected by the sampling procedures discussed in Chapter 2, Section 2.5. Eg: CUSUM Filter [...] pt_sl List[float]
Element 0, indicates the profit taking level; Element 1 is stop loss level. A non-negative float that sets the width of the two barriers. A 0 value means that the respective horizontal barrier (profit taking and/or stop loss) will be disabled.

target pd.Series
of values that are used (in conjunction with pt_sl) to determine the width of the barrier. In this program this is daily volatility series.

min_ret float
The minimum target return required for running a triple barrier search.

num_threads int
The number of threads concurrently used by the function.

vertical_barrier_times Union[pd.Series, bool]
A pandas series with the timestamps of the vertical barriers. We pass a False when we want to disable vertical barriers. [...] pt_sl = [1, 2]
min_ret = 0.005
triple_barrier_events = ml.labeling.get_events(close=data['close'],
                                               t_events=cusum_events,
                                               pt_sl=pt_sl,
                                               target=daily_vol,
                                               min_ret=min_ret,
                                               num_threads=3,
                                               vertical_barrier_times=vertical_barriers,
                                               side_prediction=data['side'])

As can be seen above, we have scaled our lower barrier and set our minimum return to 0.005.

Meta-labels can then be computed using the time that each observation touched its respective barrier.
